rounds.fact: HotBot launched in 1996 with a distinctly loud, colorful interface, and was one of the first search engines to index the full text of pages rather than just titles and keywords.
Wired magazine's website carried over its distinctive, colorful print design into the browser, standing out at a time when most news sites still looked like plain digital newspapers.
TypePad positioned itself as a more polished, professional blogging platform than free competitors, aimed at users willing to pay for more design control.
Newgrounds became the central hub for Flash animation and games in the early 2000s, launching the careers of several animators years before YouTube existed.
MSN launched alongside Windows 95 as Microsoft's answer to AOL, bundling a dial-up service with a portal homepage that shipped as the default for millions of new PCs.
